report:
The limited radial targets A–F are established as stated, with F remaining a conditional implication. I found no concrete mathematical defect. The overall verdict concerns the original completion criteria: density-zero regularity and singular or weighted-envelope regularity are expressly left unanswered. Thus this is a verified radial contribution, not a complete resolution of S06.

A. The baseline calculation is correct. Writing its local potential as Φα gives tangential eigenvalues Qα/r and radial eigenvalue Qα′. The displayed derivative dQα/dP is positive because T≥1 and 0<α<1. Radial truncations have nonnegative, increasing logarithmic slopes, so their decreasing limit is genuinely psh and retains the canonical value −∞ at o. Globally, P is smooth away from o and equals 1 on the hyperplane, where uα extends smoothly. The flux normalization is correct for the specified dd^c convention: the Fubini–Study flux is P(r)^k. Consequently the non-pluripolar baseline measure has mass 1. Near o, qα is comparable to r^(−k)L^(−1−k(1−α)); radial volume integration proves L¹ integrability and failure of every Lᵖ with p>1. Different α produce unbounded differences. The multiplier-ideal integral has exponential decay e^(−kL+tL^α), so every finite-t ideal is trivial, with no extra factor 2.

B–C. The inverse construction is valid. M′=q(P^k)′>0, Q=M^(1/k), and U′=(Q−P)/r reproduce the prescribed determinant. At infinity, a smooth radial function has a smooth expression in t=1/r: restriction to a normal complex line gives a smooth circle-invariant function of its squared radius. Thus M and Q are smooth in t, Q(0)=P(0)=1 in that coordinate, and (Q−P)/t extends smoothly. This justifies both normalization and extension along the entire hyperplane.

With b=k(1−α), the central density error gives |M−Qα^k|≤Cr^δL^(−1−b). Division by Qα^k and the positive-root expansion yield |Q−Qα|≤Cr^δL^(α−2). The exact identity Q′/Qα′=(q/qα)(Qα/Q)^(k−1) then yields the derivative estimate without differentiating the density error. Integrating R′=(Q−Qα)/r and differentiating this identity prove all three stated residual bounds. The finite residual limit establishes ordinary equivalence and the canonical pole of U. Locality of bounded truncations identifies the non-pluripolar measure everywhere outside that pole; the explicit integrable density supplies its finite total mass, so there is no missing global product theorem.

In real radius ρ=√r, the gradient and Hessian estimates are respectively Cρ^(2δ−1)L^(α−2) and Cρ^(2δ−2)L^(α−2). Radial integration proves the stated Hölder exponent. At δ=1/2 the gradient tends to zero and R−R0=o(ρ), giving C¹ extension. At δ=1 the Hessian tends to zero and the gradient is o(ρ), giving C² extension. These are extensions of the residual only; U(o) remains −∞. The radial uniqueness statement follows from Q^k=M under its explicitly imposed zero-central-flux and smoothness conditions. The competitors v_t=uα+t inf R prove membership in the actual stretching class for every finite t≥1, including the common pole and the separately handled t=1 case.

D. The flat-error argument is sound. All derivatives of a(x)=Qα(e^(−x))^k and its reciprocal have polynomial bounds for large x. The exact tail integral and its differentiated identities make E and all its derivatives decay faster than every exponential rate. Division, positive-root composition, and integration preserve this property. Conversion to ordinary r derivatives loses only fixed powers of r, which arbitrary-rate decay absorbs. The resulting smoothly flat one-variable residual composes smoothly with r=|z|².

E. The compensating annular cutoff gives exactly probability mass, and sufficiently small positive c preserves positivity globally. Near o the compensation contributes nothing to the central flux. The tail asymptotic and root expansion give precisely the two stated constants cα(1−α)/δ and cα(1−α)/δ². The radial gradient diverges for δ<1/2; a tangential real Hessian eigenvalue 2R′ diverges for δ<1. Comparison with the residual value at o excludes every larger Hölder exponent when 2δ<1. The exp(−1/r) perturbation satisfies every weighted flatness condition and remains nonzero after compensation. These are actual compact examples in unbounded, nonlogarithmic, nonminimal ordinary types, outside the listed logarithmic and minimal-Lᵖ cases.

F. Under its stated factor hypothesis, the construction is correct. Every truncation is a pullback, and the bounded product expansion leaves exactly the term with m factor directions and k projective directions, with coefficient binomial(m+k,m). Restriction to {U>−j} removes truncation-boundary contributions; increasing j gives the claimed finite measure and mass directly. No BMP hypothesis is needed for this particular calculation. Pullbacks of bounded factor potentials with masses tending to zero prove v_−(H)=0, using positivity of bounded corrected products. If h0 were closed, bounded Bedford–Taylor integration by parts would make every bounded mass equal to ∫h0^m>0: all nonconstant expansion terms are exact currents and integrate to zero. Hence h0 and H are nonclosed under the antecedent. Residual regularity and stretching competitors pull back unchanged. Existence of such a factor is neither proved nor imported; the implication establishes no unconditional nonclosed example.

The cited Demailly pages and BGL Section 2.1, including the full Proposition 2.1 proof, were freshly opened and checked. Their applications satisfy the required hypotheses. BGL Section 2.2’s BMP-dependent unbounded-product theorem is not used. No model-envelope identity, nonsymmetric uniqueness, or singularity-volume inference from one representative’s mass is used.

Harmless wording clarifications: Qα(0) denotes its limiting radial flux; R_c(0) denotes the extended residual value; the L¹/non-Lᵖ assertions concern the densities. Any description of this as “complete” must mean the complete limited radial argument. Completing the density-zero and weighted-extremal parts would require new arguments.

passages.statement: For an open set Ω⊂Cⁿ, the pointwise limit of a decreasing sequence of plurisubharmonic functions on Ω is plurisubharmonic, allowing an identically −∞ limit. Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, I.5.4.
passages.quote: For any decreasing sequence of plurisubharmonic functions uk ∈ Psh(Ω), the limit u = lim uk is plurisubharmonic on Ω.

passages.statement: On a compact complex n-fold, for 1≤p≤n, smooth real (1,1) backgrounds θ_i and bounded quasi-psh potentials φ_i admit symmetric, multilinear, non-pluripolar corrected products ∧_i(θ_i+dd^cφ_i), defined by smooth-background expansion of bounded Bedford–Taylor products. They are plurifine-local and positive when all factor currents are positive. The underlying local bounded Bedford–Taylor products are closed and continuous along decreasing bounded psh sequences with bounded limit. For potentials bounded on a compact subset K, Proposition 2.1 defines compatible restricted products through sufficiently deep bounded truncations. These assertions require no bounded mass property. Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Volumes of Bott–Chern classes, Section 2.1.
